title: C# Questions & Answers - Char Types and String Literals
sourceFile: Char Types & String Literals - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on datatypes in character and strings in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What is the size of the 'char' datatype in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the 'char' type represents a UTF-16 code unit, which is 16 bits in size.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: I am a human being c
I am a human being g

questions.explanation: The character 'g' is converted to a string and concatenated directly to the end of s1 without any added spaces. Result: 'I am a human beingg'.

questions.question: Which LINQ expression correctly converts an array of characters (days) into an array of strings to avoid casting errors?
questions.explanation: You cannot directly cast a 'char' to a 'string' because they are not inherited from each other. Using .Select(c => c.ToString()) is the standard way to perform this conversion.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday

questions.explanation: The code iterates through 'MTWFS'. Each letter is mapped via the dictionary: M->Monday, T->Tuesday, W->Wednesday, F->Friday, S->Saturday. 'R' and 'U' are not in the dayCode string.

questions.question: In the context of database types used in C# applications, which are correct differences between char and varchar?

options.text: varchar is non-unicode and char is unicode
char is fixed length, varchar is variable length
char pads shorter strings with spaces to reach set length
Both B and C are correct

questions.explanation: 'char' is fixed-length (shorter strings are padded with spaces), while 'varchar' is variable-length (stored as-is up to the maximum length).

questions.question: Which static method of the String class is used to compare two strings and determine their relationship?
questions.explanation: 'string.Compare()' is a static method used to compare two strings based on alphabetical order and culture.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The string 'Delhi' has a length of 5. The maximum valid index for the Insert method is its length (5). Attempting to insert at index 6 causes an ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

questions.question: What is the most common way to check if the content of string s1 is equal to string s2 in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the '==' operator is overloaded for the string class to perform a content-based equality check.

questions.question: What will be the output if the user enters 'BOMBAY'?
questions.explanation: The code manually reverses the string by iterating backwards through the character indices of 'BOMBAY'.

questions.question: Select the correct C# code snippet to convert a string to its Hexadecimal representation.
questions.explanation: To convert a string to hex, you first get the byte array from the string, then format each byte as a two-digit hexadecimal number (X2).

questions.question: Which logic correctly converts a Hex string back to a normal string?
questions.explanation: The 'Substring(i, 2)' takes two hex characters, which 'Convert.ToByte' then transforms into a single byte value.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: In ' I AM BEST ', index 6 is the letter 'B'. Taking 4 characters starting from 'B' (6,7,8,9) results in 'BEST'.

questions.question: Where are C# string objects stored in memory?

options.text: Depends on the length of the string

questions.explanation: Since strings are reference types in C#, the actual character data is stored on the heap, and a reference to that memory is stored on the stack.

questions.question: What is a major advantage of using a verbatim string literal (@"...") in C#?

options.text: It ignores escape sequences like '\n' or '\\'
It allows a string to span multiple lines in code
It can embed quotes using double-quotes ("")

questions.explanation: Verbatim literals make code cleaner, especially for file paths and multi-line text, because they treat backslashes as ordinary characters.

questions.question: Why are strings designed as reference types in C#?

options.text: To create them on the stack
To improve memory efficiency (via interning and reuse)

questions.explanation: By making strings reference types and immutable, the .NET runtime can optimize memory by using 'String Interning', where identical string literals share the same memory instance.
